question: Must a locally compact group acting faithfully on a manifold be a Lie group?
idea: A Lie group has a smooth, finite-dimensional group structure. The manuscript claims any locally compact second-countable group acting faithfully and continuously on the stated connected finite-dimensional topological manifold must have that structure. Faithfulness means distinct group elements act differently; the theorem includes the listed topological assumptions.
why: The study of properties of shapes preserved by continuous stretching, such as connectedness and holes.

exactClaim: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. This proves the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in all finite dimensions, for Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary.
